title: The tower is sold out and nobody lives there
description: Some of the most expensive apartments in the world are bought in order to stay empty. The lights stay off, the yearly tax on leaving them dark gets paid, and a tenant was never part of the plan.

scenes.narration: Half the windows in that tower have never been switched on.
scenes.imagePrompt: Night exterior of a very tall luxury residential tower, its glass and dark steel facade completely black and unlit from top to bottom except for a single small window glowing warm on a high floor, the vast majority of the building in total darkness, brass and bronze window mullions catching a faint reflection, the shot framed to end above the street-level entrance so no canopy or signage is visible, wet asphalt in the foreground reflecting the scarce light, deep blue-black sky, no people

scenes.narration: The units are sold. In some new towers, one address in four is nobody's daily life.
scenes.imagePrompt: Night aerial of a cluster of luxury apartment towers with bronze-trimmed glass facades and brass rooftop cornices in a city skyline, the majority of apartment windows unlit, a scattering of warm lit units, dark river and dark streets far below, cold moonlight raking across the glass

scenes.narration: A twenty-million-dollar apartment is not shelter. It is money parked where a bank statement cannot follow.
scenes.imagePrompt: Empty living room of a high-floor luxury apartment at night, floor-to-ceiling glass in brushed bronze frames, city lights far below, polished marble floor, a single leather armchair under a white dust sheet, one shaft of moonlight across the room, deep shadow in the corners

scenes.narration: Leaving it empty is not free. Taxes and charges run past a quarter million dollars a year.
scenes.imagePrompt: Underground parking level of a luxury apartment tower at night, rows of empty numbered parking bays framed in brushed steel, one car hidden under a fitted grey cover, spotless polished marble floor, a single row of overhead lights, deep shadow down the far end

scenes.narration: The owner might sleep there twelve nights out of the year.
scenes.imagePrompt: Made bed with a walnut headboard in an unused luxury apartment bedroom at night, crisp white linen without a single wrinkle, silk blackout curtains half drawn across a city view, bedside lamp switched off, cold blue light falling across the sheets, deep shadow

scenes.narration: Cities noticed. Several now tax a home left dark, a few percent of its value, every year.
scenes.imagePrompt: Extreme close facade of a luxury apartment tower at dusk photographed straight on, filling the frame with dozens of identical windows in brushed bronze mullions against pale marble spandrel panels, every single window completely dark and unlit except for exactly one glowing warm window near the center, cold blue evening light, minimal composition, no people

scenes.narration: The tax gets paid. A tenant was never the point, and would only complicate the exit.
scenes.imagePrompt: Rows of closed brass mailboxes set into a walnut-panelled wall in the dim lobby of a luxury apartment tower, one small door slightly ajar, a single overhead light raking across the polished metal, deep shadow around the edges, macro detail

scenes.narration: So the lights stay off. The building is sold out, and nobody is home.
scenes.imagePrompt: Night exterior of a tall luxury residential tower with bronze-framed glass and a marble-clad base, seen from across still black water, its facade completely black and unlit from top to bottom with no windows glowing at all, only a faint lobby glow at street level, the building mirrored in the dark water, minimal composition, no people
